comment: Shared conformance vectors for entity write-policy classification: engine/server/permissions.go (Server.checkWritePolicy) and client/src/mutations.ts (assertWritePolicy) must reach the same verdict on every case. The decision is a pure function of the write — op, and whether it asserts an expected_version — because it runs before the write transaction opens and never reads the row. `expectedVersion` is a decimal string (uint64 in Go, bigint in TS) or null for a write that asserts none; null is what makes the unguarded-PUT rule observable, and it is the case the two implementations are most likely to disagree on. `policies` gives the entity's create/update/delete policies; each is "allow" or "trustedOnly". `want` is "allow" when the write passes the schema-level check on to the app's permission policy, and "refuse" when it is rejected before that policy is consulted. Every case here is an UNTRUSTED write: a trusted one skips the check entirely, which is what "trustedOnly" is defined against.

cases.name: unrestricted entity allows every op
unrestricted entity allows PATCH
unrestricted entity allows DELETE
PATCH is an update and is refused where updates are trustedOnly
a guarded PATCH is still an update
PATCH never upserts, so create policy does not reach it
PATCH asserting version 0 is still an update, not a create
DELETE is refused where deletes are trustedOnly
DELETE is unaffected by create and update policies
PUT asserting version 0 is provably a create and is refused where creates are trustedOnly
PUT asserting version 0 is a create, so update policy does not reach it
PUT asserting a non-zero version is provably an update and is refused where updates are trustedOnly
PUT asserting a non-zero version is an update, so create policy does not reach it
unguarded PUT is refused where creates are trustedOnly, since it would create an absent row
unguarded PUT is refused where updates are trustedOnly, since it would replace a present row
unguarded PUT is refused where both are trustedOnly
unguarded PUT passes where neither create nor update is restricted, whatever delete says
server-owned entity refuses a guarded create
append-only entity admits a guarded create
append-only entity refuses an edit
an unspecified op is left to the write path to reject
